rows.grounds: bahuvrīhi/tatpuruṣa compound qualifying the fuel-sticks; produced from trees that yield milky sap
fused sandhi form containing samidbhiḥ (instrumental plural of samidh), dūrvayā (instrumental singular of dūrvā), and athavā (alternative particle)
repetition of the alternative dūrvayā athavā as given in the text; dūrvā in instrumental singular with athavā

items.question: What alternative materials may serve as fuel to complete the fire offering?
premises: The fire offering is to be completed after the preceding offerings.
Fuel-sticks born from milk-yielding trees are a suitable material.
Dūrvā grass is presented as an alternative material.
items.inference: The fire offering may be completed using fuel-sticks from milk-yielding trees or, alternatively, using dūrvā grass.
uncertainties: The repetition of dūrvayāthavā in the third token may be emphatic or a textual duplication; its exact rhetorical function is unclear.
items.plain_english: One should complete the fire offering with fuel-sticks produced from milk-yielding trees, or alternatively with dūrvā grass.
